title: The stones nobody could lift
question: How Did Humans Move Stones Weighing Over 1,000 Tons?
scoredBy: inspection of rendered frames at 0/33/66/94 per shot
verdict: Fourteen shots now carry the block: standing on the ground line, measured against a human figure drawn at a stated height, on rollers that turn at the speed it travels, with ropes leaving the frame forward and a force arrow labelled NO CRANE. The size is derived from the person rather than asserted, which is the only way a drawing can make a thousand tons mean anything. The plate says ILLUSTRATIVE RECONSTRUCTION -- METHOD UNCERTAIN, because it is.
whatWorked: Scale is done properly: a marked human-height bar and a silhouette beside the load, so the block's size is read off the figure instead of being claimed.
The rollers turn at the speed the load moves. If they did not, the drawing would be contradicting itself, and that is checkable.
The load moves slowly and never arrives, which is what 'a few feet an hour, for months' means. A block crossing the frame would have contradicted the narration.
The uncertainty is stated in the weaker form. Nobody knows how the trilithon was moved, and SCHEMATIC RECONSTRUCTION would have claimed otherwise.
The quarry line correctly took a map rather than a haulage drawing -- it is about where the stone came from, not about moving it.

whatFailed.what: The counter read 576.377 TONS on its way to 800.
whatFailed.why: The component used a raw float interpolation instead of the repo's shared integer counter. Fixed; it now lands exactly, as law 27 requires everywhere else.

whatFailed.what: The ropes leave the frame but nothing is pulling them.
whatFailed.why: True to the claim -- the capstans were off-picture -- but it means the force is implied rather than shown.

whatFailed.what: ash-grey over a drawn ground is still nearly black.
whatFailed.why: The drawn ground was designed as a bed for a photograph that would supply the tone.

gatesFailed: no photograph anywhere in the reel — every shot is drawn or typeset
